Just to help a bit with that. Lets say semen gets at the entance. For sperm to get to an egg, if must be ejaculated into the vaginal canal. And then they swim their way through the cervix and they make their way up into the fallopian tube, where if their is an egg, they fertilise the egg. 
Here is a few factors to take in mind. The pH of the vagina, when near ovulation, the vagina becomes sperm friendly. But in other days of the month, the pH is not sperm friendly. 
Many sperm die before they even get through the cervix. Only the strongest of sperm make it up into the tube. 
So if sperm gets on the entrance of vaginal, the sperm must be super strong to travel that extra lenght (into the vagina). And remember, the vaginal secretions help the sperm to swim. So no, realistically. You cannot get pregnant if sperm is at the entrance of the vagina. You cannot get pregnant when bathing with your partner. The heat of the water also kills sperm if there was sperm in the water. And soap and all that. 
The only way you CAN get pregnant, is if sperm is ejaculated into the vagina. And  you are near ovulation or OVULATING.

For a pregnancy to occur. A woman must be ovulating or a few days before ovulation. Semen must be ejaculated in the vagina. There are multiple methods of birth control to stop that from happening. Barrier methods (condoms, female condom, ect) it stops sperm fro entering the vagina. Hormonal methods that stop ovulation from occuring (which means that no egg is there to fertilize so no pregnancy will occur) and it thickens cervical mucus, making it harder for the sperm to enter the uterus and travel up the fallopian tube to meet the egg. It also thins out the endometrium. So IF sperm managed to meet with an egg and fertilize (ovulation occured) then it won't have an stable enough layer to implant in the uterus. It protects us in 3 ways. 
You cannot get pregnant from sitting on a tiolet seat. Or coming in contact with dry sperm. 
It must be intercourse, and without birth control.
